decisions.reason: The reference-class electrometer is a core dosimetry instrument featured on the home page for two consecutive years, reflecting heavy development investment and visible public commitment central to the firm's direction.

The oncology risk management software has its own page and represents a sunk software investment in the firm's announced move into clinical workflow solutions, so any slow uptake is likely attributed to temporary adoption hurdles.
The CT phantom was launched only in 2024 and fits the firm's imaging QA line, so it is too early to judge and recent investment favors persistence.
The mammography phantom is a fresh 2024 launch within a deliberate expansion into imaging QA, and management will justify its continuation despite partial overlap with Product E.
The full-field mammography phantom is newly launched with its own page and is tied to regulatory QA demand, so commitment to the new imaging portfolio keeps it on the market.
The broad medical imaging QA instrument line embodies the firm's announced strategic direction, making withdrawal very unlikely.
